summary: Streaming responses cut off with 504s when prefix length + max_tokens load is high
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that streaming generations terminate mid-response with gateway 504 and no finalization when the sum of input prefix tokens and max_tokens crosses ~180k tokens. Impact: Several production endpoints for NarrateAI experience failed story generations, causing degraded user experience and increased support volume. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east, pinned model redwood-v2-13B-quant, burstable reserved capacity. Behavior is intermittent but reproducible with very large prompts plus high max_tokens (customer uses long context + extended generation).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer API key on prod us-east dedicated endpoint.
2) Send a streaming generation request with ~120k token prefix (serialized docs) and max_tokens=80k.
3) Observe streaming chunks for ~30-90s then finalization never arrives and upstream gateway returns 504 to client.
4) Repeat with smaller combined token budget (<=100k) — completes normally.
5) Reproduce intermittently: sometimes generation completes but final chunk delayed by >60s before 504 timeout.
observed_behavior: Client receives partial stream chunks, then a gateway-level 504 after ~90s. The runtime shows the worker still computing (high GPU utilization) but the API gateway connection has closed. No deterministic KV-cache eviction shown in immediate logs.
expected_behavior: Streaming completes with final chunk and HTTP 200, or graceful fallback to a lower-latency model variant without producing a gateway 504. The system should surface progress or graceful abort instead of abrupt connection drop.
logs_snippets: [2026-02-12T14:03:21Z] gateway: upstream response timeout after 90s for request id=req-9a4f
[2026-02-12T14:03:22Z] stream-handler: client connection closed by gateway id=gw-11
[2026-02-12T14:03:23Z] scheduler: no autoscale event triggered; pod remained at single instance
investigation_notes: Support verified reproducibility with NarrateAI test key and sample payload (privileged support run).
SRE captured runtime stack traces: CPU thread handling finalization blocked on a large allreduce-like memcpy path in quant kernel under extreme KV activity.
Hypothesis 1: Kernel path for large context + high max_tokens interacts poorly with continuous batching causing single-request tail latency spike.
Hypothesis 2: Gateway timeout is fixed at 90s in fronting layer; long tail compute occasionally exceeds this even though worker will finish soon after — causing client-observed 504s.
Observed that KV-cache size grew and occasional garbage collection pause (~200-400ms) occurred, but not large enough to explain 90s timeout by itself.
Checked autoscaling: Dedicated pool min=1 max=3; during reproductions pool stayed at 1 — no immediate scaling triggered by queue depth threshold.

resolution: Workaround applied: gateway upstream timeout increased from 90s to 180s for the customer's dedicated route and an alert was created to detect >120s tail latency. Engineering PR to async-ify the bigint memcpy in quantized kernel created and linked (see PR). Long-term: kernel fix merged in canary and scheduled for rollout next maintenance window; autoscaler thresholds will be adjusted to trigger earlier scale-up on queue depth for dedicated pools. Customer validated generation success after timeout increase and reported reduced user-facing errors.
